evidence: The paper uses Quick Permutation Test (QuiPT) for n-gram feature selection before random forest training: "To select the informative n-grams, we performed Quick Permutation Test (QuiPT) [37]...with p-value threshold 0.0001. We obtained 1883 informative n-grams and used them for CancerGram training." Results report only classifier performance metrics (accuracy, AU1U, Kappa) on validation and independent test sets; no variable importance scores, rankings, or p-values appear in any table or figure. Conclusions discuss empirically observed amino acid composition differences, validated via held-out test performance, not random forest feature importance magnitudes.
